references.text: The preceding verse describes how the Levite's concubine was found lying at the door in the morning, which provides context for his command to get up.
Abraham placed wood on the donkey before he went to Mount Moriah, a parallel to how the Levite placed his dead concubine on the donkey to travel home.
The Levite later told the tribes of Israel what had happened to his concubine and how he brought her home.
The prophet took up the slain man and laid him on a donkey to bring him back, an action parallel to the Levite's transport of his dead concubine.
